sample_unit: expert quality evaluations of LLM responses

links.outcome: Expert-rated quality and potential harmfulness of LLM answers to hyperthermia clinical and physics questions
links.effect: Mean quality 3.26 (DeepSeek), 3.18 (Llama), 3.07 (GPT-4o); potentially harmful in 17.8%, 19.3%, 15.3% of cases; ~25% rated bad to very bad.
links.quote: Notably, despite “acceptable” mean scores, approximately 25% of responses were rated “bad” to “very bad,” and potentially harmful answers occurred in ∼15–19% of evaluations, indicating a non-trivial risk if used without domain expertise.

links.outcome: LLM performance on specialized clinical domain questions despite general expert-level benchmark claims
links.effect: Despite expert-level performance in many medical domains, the three LLMs achieved only 'acceptable' mean quality (3.07-3.26) in moderate hyperthermia, with 15-19% potentially harmful answers.
links.quote: Our findings indicate that the performance of LLMs in HT in versions available at the time of investigation is only partially satisfactory.

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the performance and clinical safety/harmfulness of three LLMs answering open-ended medical questions regarding moderate hyperthermia, evaluated offline by expert panels without testing specific deployment practices.
